title: Netflix Adopts Cloud-Native Job Queueing System Kueue to Replace an In-House Solution
gist: Netflix has migrated most of its batch workloads off Compute Managed Batch (CMB), the in-house scheduler it built for its Titus container platform in 2018, onto the open-source Kubernetes-native queueing system Kueue — a concrete data point that the Kubernetes ecosystem has now absorbed enough capability to make bespoke infrastructure at hyperscale uneconomic. API parity was the derisking mechanism, and preemption-based fair sharing has already lifted average resource utilization.

insights.claim: Netflix has migrated most of its batch workloads from its homegrown Compute Managed Batch system to the open-source Kubernetes-native scheduler Kueue, and is now running millions of batch workloads in production on it.
insights.speaker: Rafał Gancarz
insights.so_what: A hyperscale reference customer legitimises Kueue as the default batch layer on Kubernetes — relevant to anyone selling proprietary batch schedulers.
insights.quote: Netflix is currently managing millions of batch workloads in production using Kueue, but the migration is still underway.
insights.locator: Netflix is currently managing millions of batch workloads

insights.claim: The trigger for abandoning in-house infrastructure was that open-source Kubernetes projects absorbed most of the differentiating features Netflix built into CMB after 2018, eroding the return on maintaining a bespoke system.
insights.speaker: Rafał Gancarz
insights.so_what: The commoditization clock on custom infra is roughly seven years here — a useful heuristic for valuing any 'proprietary platform' moat in cloud-native tooling.
insights.quote: The company observed that since CMB’s creation in 2018, many of its key features have been incorporated into open-source projects that evolved within the Kubernetes ecosystem.
insights.locator: The company observed that since CMB’s creation in 2018

insights.claim: A second driver was that loose Kubernetes integration made shipping new features in CMB progressively harder, so the in-house system carried a rising development tax rather than just a maintenance cost.
insights.speaker: Rafał Gancarz
insights.so_what: Velocity decay, not raw cost, is the argument that kills internal platforms — the same logic applies to any non-native fork of a fast-moving ecosystem.
insights.quote: Additionally, developing new features in CMB has become more difficult as the solution wasn’t as tightly integrated with Kubernetes.
insights.locator: The company observed that since CMB’s creation in 2018

insights.claim: Netflix's stated selection criteria for Kueue were extensive capabilities and flexibility, wide adoption, and pace of innovation — ecosystem momentum weighed alongside features.
insights.speaker: Rafał Gancarz
insights.so_what: Large enterprises now explicitly price 'pace of innovation' of an OSS project into procurement, favouring projects with dense contributor bases over feature-complete but static ones.
insights.quote: engineers decided to opt for Kueue as a replacement for CMB, due to its extensive capabilities and flexibility, wide adoption, and pace of innovation
insights.locator: In the end, engineers decided to opt for Kueue

insights.claim: Maintaining API parity between the old and new systems was the primary derisking device, letting Netflix migrate gradually and keep the change fully transparent to existing CMB users.
insights.speaker: Rafał Gancarz
insights.so_what: A reusable playbook for replatforming: freeze the interface, swap the engine — the pattern that makes large infra swaps financeable.
insights.quote: Engineers highlighted that maintaining API parity while migrating underlying components derisked the project significantly and offered a seamless end-user experience.
insights.locator: Engineers highlighted that maintaining API parity

insights.claim: Netflix deliberately migrated its largest and most complex customer first rather than last, and credits that sequencing with a production migration that lasted only four weeks.
insights.speaker: Rafał Gancarz
insights.so_what: Inverts the standard low-risk-first migration norm; the counterintuitive ordering is the transferable lesson for any platform team budgeting a cutover.
insights.quote: This allowed us to build confidence that we could later migrate other customers to Netflix Batch without issues, and resulted in the production migration lasting only 4 weeks.
insights.locator: Don’t wait until the end to migrate the most complex use case

insights.claim: The migration was made tenant-bound with easy rollback, and CMB's tenant hierarchy was mapped onto Kueue primitives — internal tenants to Cohorts, leaf tenants to a ClusterQueue and LocalQueue pair, with resource flavors and nominal quotas carrying over capacity configuration.
insights.speaker: Rafał Gancarz
insights.so_what: Kueue's abstractions were rich enough to absorb a hyperscaler's multi-tenant capacity model without custom extension — a strong signal of project maturity.
insights.quote: Engineers mapped internal tenants in CMB to Cohors in Kueue and leaf tenants to a pair of ClusterQueue and LocalQueue resources.
insights.locator: Engineers mapped internal tenants in CMB

insights.claim: Load testing in a non-production environment was used to tune performance configuration so the replacement could meet required container launch rate and maximum throughput from day one, rather than degrading gradually in production.
insights.speaker: Rafał Gancarz
insights.so_what: Throughput parity was treated as a launch gate, not a post-migration optimization — the discipline that separates successful infra swaps from stalled ones.
insights.quote: They also explained that running load tests in the non-prod environment helped them fine-tune performance-related configuration options to meet the platform’s throughput requirements.
insights.locator: They also explained that running load tests

insights.claim: Adopting preemption-based fair sharing let Netflix significantly improve average resource utilization by lending idle capacity between tenants while preserving reservation semantics — a capability the article implies would have been costly to build in-house.
insights.speaker: Rafał Gancarz
insights.so_what: Fleet utilization gains at Netflix scale translate directly into avoided compute spend; the same lever is available to any large Kubernetes batch estate.
insights.quote: engineers were able to significantly improve average resource utilization by leveraging preemption-based fair sharing to maintain reservation semantics while lending idle capacity to other tenants
insights.locator: More recently, engineers were able to significantly improve

insights.claim: Netflix's justification includes benefiting from features that would have been costly to incorporate into the homegrown solution, framing the migration as an option on the open-source roadmap rather than a like-for-like replacement.
insights.speaker: Rafał Gancarz
insights.so_what: The real ROI case for adopting OSS infra is the unbuilt roadmap you inherit for free — the argument to test when evaluating any build-vs-adopt decision.
insights.quote: The company mapped the capabilities previously created in-house to Kueue’s functionality and also benefited from new features that would have been costly to incorporate into its homegrown solution.
insights.locator: Netflix migrated most of its batch workloads onto Kueue
